lawyer: Sharif Uddin Chaklader, Advocate — For the Petitioner.
parties:
Abdul Awal and others ------ Petitioners
Vs.
Jebon Nahar ------ Opposite Party
full_judgment:
This Rule has been issued at the instance of the plaintiff-landlord, against the judgment and decree passed in SCC Suit 1 of 1992, dated 22-2-1995. The suit was filed for ejectment of the opposite party Jebun Nahar as monthly tenant from the suit premises being Commercial Plot No.39, Block Kha, main road No. 1 section 9, Mirpur (sic) of defendants default in payment of rent, expiry of the period of lease according to the deed of argeement creating lease and also for bonafide and personal requirement of the premises by the plaintiff landlord. The defendant opposite party was inducted as a monthly tenant for 4 years in the suit premises on and from 1-1-83 affixing monthly rent at Taka 1000.00 only. It is also on evidence that the tenant defendant paid Taka 50,000.00 as advance rent on condition that Taka 300.00 would be adjusted from every month''s rent. Accordingly the tenant was to pay Taka 700.00 per month as rent for the tenanted shop. Later on the enire building along with the tenanted shop room was sold by Akhter Jahan Murshida Begum, the previous landlord of the defendant tenant, to the present plaintiff and delivered constructive possession to purchaser, present plaintiff. Plaintiff's allegation is that the tenant stopped payment of rent from the month of June 1986 on the ground that said Akhter Jahan Murshida Begum had entered into an agreement to sell the suit premises to the tenant defendant at Taka 3,00,000.00 (three lakh) only. Tenant paid Taka 1,00,000.00 (One lakh) as advance towards the said consideration money. But the seller did not execute and register the necessary sale deed in respect of the shop room to the tenant as per deed of agreement, so she stopped payment of rent from the month of June, 1986. Subsequently, on 29-9-88 original owner, said Akhter Jahan Murshida Begum transferred the suit premises by way of sale to the present plaintiffs ignoring the agreement with the defendant. The sale was effected during tenancy of the defendant. After purchase of the suit premises the present plaintiffs orally attorned the tenant defendant about their purchase and also demanded rent. But the defendant did not pay rent. Hence after service of notice under section 106 of the Transfer Property Act the suit has been filed. the defendant received the notice. The entire amount of advance money of Taka 50,000.00 paid by the tenant has not been exhausted. So according to the defendant tenant the plaintiff can not evict her as prayed for at the present stage and in the present suit. She admits that the payment of rent has been stopped, because the deed of sale as agreed upon has not been executed and registered by the landlord. In this context both parties led evidence. Trial Court dismissed the suit by his impugned judgment and decree. The plaintiff has come up with this Revision and obtained the Rule. Trial Court found that the tenant is a defaulter as he has not paid rent from the month of June, 1986. The original agreement for tenancy was created for 4 years which also has expired, was not renewed, now new agreement for tenancy has been made between the parties. But the trial Court held that until adjustment of the entire money which was paid as advance of Taka 300.00 per month as was agreed upon, she can not be evicted. It is alleged by the tenant that the lady having refused to accept the rent from the tenant the same is being, deposited in the House Rent Controller office in Case No. 474 of 1986. 

 5. Accordingly, the Rule is made absolute, the suit is decreed, The defendant shall, be evicted from the suit premises in accordance with law, through execution of the decree, if the defendant does not vacate from the suit premises within 6(six) months from the date of receipt of this judgment by the trial Court.
